title: Flat direct image and the derived coherator: normalized interchange
statement:
Let $f:Z\to Y$ be a flat quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]; quasi-compact means that inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Write $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal O_T)$, and let $I_T\dashv C_T$ with unit $e_T$ and counit $d_T$ be [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-coherator-adjunction] for $T=Z,Y$. All derived categories are unbounded. Let $P_f:D(\mathcal A_Y)\to D(\mathcal A_Z)$ be termwise tensor pullback, and let $R_f=Rf_*:D(\mathcal O_Z)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$ be module derived direct image [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. The functor $f_*:\mathcal A_Z\to\mathcal A_Y$ has a total right derived functor $\Phi_f$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], and $P_f\dashv\Phi_f$; write $u_f:\operatorname{id}\to\Phi_fP_f$ for its induced derived unit. Tensor pullback on all modules is exact and its derived functor is left adjoint to $R_f$, with unit $v_f$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $\lambda:C_YR_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_fC_Z$, obtained by identifying these as right adjoints to $I_ZP_f=f^*I_Y$. All these functors and adjunctions carry the canonical triangulated and shift-compatible structures. Suppose $c:I_Y\Phi_f\xrightarrow{\sim}R_fI_Z$ is a natural isomorphism whose composite with the localized right-derived comparison unit of $f_*$ is the canonical module-derived comparison, computed using a K-injective module resolution. Then, with composition read right to left and the exact pullback/inclusion identifications understood, one has for all $B\in D(\mathcal A_Z)$, $E\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ and $H\in D(\mathcal A_Y)$:
$$\lambda_{I_ZB}\circ C_Y(c_B)\circ e_Y(\Phi_fB)=\Phi_f(e_Z(B)),$$
$$d_Y(R_fE)=R_f(d_Z(E))\circ c_{C_ZE}\circ I_Y(\lambda_E),$$
$$c_{P_fH}\circ I_Y(u_f(H))=v_f(I_YH).$$
In particular these assertions apply when $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f$ is the inclusion of any affine open of $Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion].

proof.text: By the quasi-coherent pushforward theorem, $f_*$ restricts to $F:\mathcal A_Z\to\mathcal A_Y$, since $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence and is exact on all modules because $f$ is flat. Exactness of the inclusions therefore makes its restriction $P^0:\mathcal A_Y\to\mathcal A_Z$ exact as well. Fullness of these abelian subcategories restricts the ordinary module Hom bijection to $P^0\dashv F$. Thus $i_ZP^0=f^*i_Y$ and $i_YF=f_*i_Z$, and these two identifications respect adjuncts: a module map and its transpose are literally the same maps as in the full quasi-coherent subcategories.

source.place: Tag 08D8, lemma-flat-pushforward-coherator, first two proof paragraphs; schemes.tex Tag 01LC and modules.tex Tags 01BG, 02N4

proof.text: Both $\mathcal A_Z$ and the scheme module category $\mathcal M_Z$ are Grothendieck abelian, so every complex in either category has a K-injective resolution. Applying $F$ degreewise induces an exact functor on homotopy categories: it takes the cone of $a$ to the cone of $F(a)$ because an additive functor preserves the finite biproducts and signed matrices defining a cone. The enough-K-injectives theorem therefore gives its total unbounded right derived functor $\Phi_f$, computed by $F(J)$ on K-injective $J$. The exact-functor factorization gives the termwise derived $P_f$, and the derived-adjunction theorem applied to $P^0\dashv F$ gives $P_f\dashv\Phi_f$ with its induced unit $u_f$. Use the module derived adjunction for $f^*\dashv f_*$; flat exactness identifies its left functor with termwise $f^*$, giving the stated unit $v_f$.

source.place: Tag 08D8, proof paragraphs constructing Phi and the two derived pullback adjunctions; injectives.tex Tag 079P; derived.tex Tags 070K, 070Y, 09T5

proof.text:
Write $K=f^*$ on the module derived categories, $P=P_f$, $\Phi=\Phi_f$, $R=R_f$, and write $w:P\Phi\to\operatorname{id}$ and $\epsilon:KR\to\operatorname{id}$ for the two counits. Compose adjunction Hom bijections to obtain, for $H\in D(\mathcal A_Y)$ and $E\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(H,C_YRE)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(I_YH,RE)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(KI_YH,E)=\operatorname{Hom}(I_ZPH,E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(PH,C_ZE)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,\Phi C_ZE).$$
The composite-adjunction definition gives these as two adjunctions to $I_ZP=KI_Y$. Uniqueness of right adjoints gives their canonical natural isomorphism $\lambda:C_YR\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi C_Z$. Its defining counit equation, using that definition, is
$$d_Z(E)\,I_Z(w_{C_ZE})\,I_ZP(\lambda_E)=\epsilon_E\,K(d_Y(RE)).\tag{*}$$
Here and below juxtaposition denotes composition read right to left.

source.place: Tag 08D8, four Hom identifications in the last proof paragraph; categories.tex Tag 0037, adjunction formulas

proof.text:
Apply the exact-square right-derived-unit theorem with $F=f_*|_{\mathcal A_Z}$, $G=f_*$ on modules, $U=i_Z$ and $V=i_Y$, and with the identity ordinary square $i_YF=Gi_Z$. The inclusions are exact, and both source categories have K-injective resolutions by step 2. It follows that $I_Y\Phi$, with its localized comparison unit, is a right derived functor of $i_YF$. The assumed normalization of $c$ is precisely the characterizing equation for the theorem's unique comparison $b:I_Y\Phi\to RI_Z$. Consequently $c=b$. Now apply the normalized derived-adjoint-square theorem to the ordinary compatible adjunction square of step 1, with $L=P^0$, $R=F$, $L_0=f^*$, $R_0=f_*$, $V=i_Z$ and $W=i_Y$. Its unit equation gives
$$c_{PH}\,I_Y(u_f(H))=v_f(I_YH),$$
and its counit equation gives
$$I_Z(w_B)=\epsilon_{I_ZB}\,K(c_B).\tag{**}$$
This proves the third requested identity and pins down the counit needed below. The comparison theorem does not require $i_Z$ to preserve K-injectives.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors, with Tag 070Y; normalized exact-square consequences stated in the two cited nodes

proof.text:
For the first identity, apply the Hom bijection in step 3 at $H=\Phi B$ and $E=I_ZB$ to the map $C_Y(c_B)e_Y(\Phi B):\Phi B\to C_YRI_ZB$. Its successive inverse transposes first give $c_B:I_Y\Phi B\to RI_ZB$ (the $I_Y\dashv C_Y$ triangle identity), and then $\epsilon_{I_ZB}K(c_B)=I_Z(w_B)$ by (**). On the other side, the inverse transpose of $\Phi(e_Z(B)):\Phi B\to\Phi C_ZI_ZB$ under $P\dashv\Phi$ is $e_Z(B)w_B$, by counit naturality. Its further inverse transpose under $I_Z\dashv C_Z$ is $d_Z(I_ZB)I_Z(e_Z(B))I_Z(w_B)=I_Z(w_B)$ by the triangle identity. Since $\lambda$ identifies these two Hom bijections, their common inverse transpose proves
$$\lambda_{I_ZB}\,C_Y(c_B)\,e_Y(\Phi B)=\Phi(e_Z(B)).$$

source.place: Tag 08D8, explicit evaluation of the four Hom identifications on e_Y; categories.tex Tag 0037, counit naturality and triangle identities

proof.text:
For the second identity, take inverse transposes under $K\dashv R$. The inverse transpose of $d_Y(RE)$ is $\epsilon_EK(d_Y(RE))$. The inverse transpose of $R(d_Z(E))c_{C_ZE}I_Y(\lambda_E)$ is, by naturality of $\epsilon$,
$$d_Z(E)\,\epsilon_{I_ZC_ZE}\,K(c_{C_ZE})\,KI_Y(\lambda_E).$$
Using (**) with $B=C_ZE$ and $KI_Y=I_ZP$, this becomes $d_Z(E)I_Z(w_{C_ZE})I_ZP(\lambda_E)$, which equals the first inverse transpose by (*). Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection proves exactly
$$d_Y(RE)=R(d_Z(E))\,c_{C_ZE}\,I_Y(\lambda_E).$$

source.place: Tag 08D8, explicit evaluation of the composite counits; categories.tex Tag 0037, inverse transpose and naturality

proof.text: The exact-functor factorization equips $I_T$, $P$ and $K$ with their canonical triangulated structures and integer-shift comparisons. The K-injective right-derived-functor theorem supplies those structures for $C_T$, $\Phi$ and $R$. The coherator node already includes compatibility of $e_T,d_T$ with shifts. Apply canonical right-derived adjunction shift compatibility to the exact left adjoints $P^0$ and $f^*$ to obtain the same compatibility for $u_f,w,v_f,\epsilon$, retaining the fixed K-injective shifts. Finally the composite Hom bijections commute with shifts, because each of their units and counits does. Their defining characterization of $\lambda$ then gives its shift compatibility: shifting either inverse transpose produces the same shifted map. Thus all constructions use the canonical structures appearing in the statement.

source.place: Tags 014X, 015F, 070K, 070Y, 09T5; canonical shift compatibility as stated in lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift

proof.text: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an affine open with $Y$ qcqs. Both $U$ and every affine open $V\subseteq Y$ are quasi-compact. The quasi-separated-intersection theorem makes $j^{-1}(V)=U\cap V$ quasi-compact; this is precisely quasi-compactness of $j$. By the open-immersion definition its stalk maps are isomorphisms, so are flat. Its diagonal $U\to U\times_YU$ is an isomorphism: the inverse is either projection, since a map into the fibre product is a pair of maps into $U$ agreeing in the open subspace of $Y$, hence an equal pair. The diagonal is consequently quasi-compact, and $j$ is quasi-separated. All hypotheses already used for $f$ hold for $j$, including the empty affine open. This proves the final specialization.
